D.tier: Queued, roster and office levers only

D.t: David Jolly trails by 3.9 and wins 24% of simulations. Closing it takes about 175,716 voters switching sides, or 351,432 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +11.7 and D +4.2. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +2.9. Your best recent poll is Change Research at D +0.8; your worst is YouGov for N+ Univision at R +9.1. 22 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Broward, a projected net 212,612 votes; Orange, a projected net 89,782 votes; Palm Beach, a projected net 76,368 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Miami-Dade, D +0.7, 9.5% of the vote; Hillsborough, D +7.4, 6.3% of the vote; Pinellas, D +8.5, 5.1% of the vote; Duval, D +4.9, 4.4% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, David Jolly runs furthest behind in Collier, Osceola, Lee. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 79% of voters, 51 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.96 points; White voters, 69% of voters, 41 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.46 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 68% of voters, 47 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.38 points.
The forecast's worst groups for David Jolly: Immigration voters 16 to 83, Midsize counties 40 to 59, White voters 41 to 57. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$6.0M cash against $44.0M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Registered Democrats cast 38% of the 4,717,903 ballots in Florida so far, against 41% for the other party. That is 7.3 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 2.1 points away from David Jolly. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Cash: $44.0M in the bank against $6.0M for David Jolly.

R.t: Byron Donalds leads by 3.9 in the forecast and wins 76% of simulations. The cushion is about 351,432 votes; a one point swing is about 44,711 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +4.2 and R +11.7. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +2.9. Your best recent poll is YouGov for N+ Univision at R +9.1; your worst is Change Research at D +0.8. 22 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Lee, a projected net 82,790 votes; Collier, a projected net 56,575 votes; Marion, a projected net 42,875 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Miami-Dade, D +0.7, 9.5% of the vote; Hillsborough, D +7.4, 6.3% of the vote; Pinellas, D +8.5, 5.1% of the vote; Duval, D +4.9, 4.4% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Byron Donalds runs furthest behind in Pinellas, Hernando, Broward. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 79% of voters, 48 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.96 points; White voters, 69% of voters, 57 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.46 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 68% of voters, 51 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.38 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Byron Donalds: Black voters 19 to 79, Independents 28 to 69, Moderates 32 to 65. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$44.0M cash against $6.0M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
